q.s: Which of the following is the largest Harappan site located within the present-day territory of India?
q.x: Rakhigarhi in Haryana is the largest Harappan site in India; Dholavira in Gujarat is the second largest.

q.s: Which Harappan site is regarded as the largest site of the civilisation in present-day Pakistan?
q.x: Mohenjodaro in Sindh is the largest Harappan site in Pakistan; Ganweriwala is also among the five largest sites.

q.s: At which Harappan site was a dog found buried along with a human in an oval pit?
q.x: The burial of a dog with a human in an oval pit comes from Ropar in Punjab, not Lothal.

q.s: A cemetery of about 125 graves, aligned north–south, was excavated at which site in Uttar Pradesh?
q.x: Sanauli in Baghpat district of Uttar Pradesh yielded a cemetery of about 125 north–south graves.

q.s: The famous bronze 'Dancing Girl' of the Harappan civilisation was cast using which technique?
q.x: The Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro was cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) method, showing advanced metallurgy.

q.s: Who among the following is associated with elaborating the Aryan invasion theory of the decline of the Harappan civilisation?
q.x: Wheeler (1947) elaborated the Aryan invasion theory first put forward by Ramaprasad Chanda (1926); Sahni, Rao and Marshall linked the decline to floods.

q.s: The Kannada work 'Kavirajamarga' is attributed to which of the following rulers?
q.x: Kavirajamarga, the earliest available Kannada work on poetics, is attributed to the Rashtrakuta king Amoghavarsha I.

q.s: Who among the following is the author of 'Brihat Samhita', an encyclopaedic work on astronomy and other subjects?
q.x: Varahamihira wrote the Brihat Samhita; Rajasekhara wrote Kavyamimamsa.

q.s: A field site spanning the Satavahana to Vijayanagara periods was found in 2026 in which tiger reserve?
q.x: The site was reported from the Nallamala Tiger Reserve region spanning the Satavahana to Vijayanagara periods.

q.s: In the Rigveda, the term 'Mujavant' refers to which of the following?
q.x: Mujavant was a mountain in the Hindu Kush region known for soma; Himavant is the Himalayas and Dhanva desert land.

q.s: Which crop is regarded as the chief cereal crop of the Rigvedic period?
q.x: Yava (barley) was the chief Rigvedic crop; vrihi (rice) and godhuma (wheat) are named only in later Vedic texts.

q.s: The coins bearing a ship with two masts, showing maritime trade, are attributed to which Satavahana ruler?
q.x: The ship-mast coins belong to Yajna Sri Satakarni; the Satavahanas also struck coins of lead.

q.s: Which of the following dynasties is known for issuing a large number of coins made of lead?
q.x: The Satavahanas issued many lead coins along with copper and potin; gold coins in large numbers came with the Kushanas.

q.s: Parshvanatha, the twenty-third Jain Tirthankara, was born at which of the following places?
q.x: Parshvanatha was born at Varanasi to King Asvasena and Queen Vama; he attained nirvana at Sammed Shikhar.

q.s: Sammed Shikhar, the Jain pilgrimage centre where several Tirthankaras attained nirvana, is located in which state?
q.x: Sammed Shikhar is on Parasnath hill in Jharkhand; Udayagiri–Khandagiri is in Odisha and the Dilwara temples in Rajasthan.

q.s: The Dilwara group of Jain temples is located at which of the following places?
q.x: The marble Dilwara temples are at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.

q.s: According to Jain tradition, Chandragupta Maurya died by Sallekhana at which of the following places?
q.x: Jain tradition says Chandragupta went south with Bhadrabahu and died by Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola in Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following was the main port of the Ganga basin on the east coast during the Mauryan period?
q.x: Tamralipti in Bengal was the east-coast port; Bharukachchha (Broach) and Sopara were on the west coast.

q.s: Which historian called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' because of his many conquests?
q.x: V.A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India'.

q.s: Which Gupta ruler bore the title 'Mahendraditya'?
q.x: Kumaragupta I was Mahendraditya; Chandragupta II bore the title Vikramaditya.

q.s: Which ancient text written by Vagbhata is an important work on Ayurveda?
q.x: Vagbhata wrote the Ashtanga Sangraha and Ashtanga Hridaya; Hastyayurveda on elephant diseases is linked with Palakapya.

q.s: Muhammad bin Tughlaq created the department 'Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi' for which purpose?
q.x: Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi was his agriculture department meant to bring waste land under cultivation.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the loans given to peasants for seeds and digging wells were called:
q.x: Taqavi or sondhar loans were state advances to cultivators for seeds and wells.

q.s: In the First Battle of Panipat (1526), Babur's artillery was handled by Ustad Ali Quli and:
q.x: Babur's artillery and musketeers were commanded by Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa, which Ibrahim Lodi lacked.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the Diwan-i-Wizarat headed by the Wazir mainly dealt with:
q.x: The Diwan-i-Wizarat dealt with finance, revenue, accounts and allotment of iqtas.

q.s: In the Qutb Shahi administration of Golconda, the Mir Jumla was:
o: The chief minister in charge of finance
The head of the royal household
q.x: The Qutb Shahi Mir Jumla was the chief minister in charge of finance, not the army commander.

q.s: Under the Delhi Sultanate, the holder of an iqta was known as:
q.x: The holder of an iqta was the muqti or iqtadar; the iqta is the ancestor of the Mughal jagir.

q.s: The Hindi Sufi epic 'Padmavat' was written by which of the following poets?
q.x: Malik Muhammad Jayasi wrote Padmavat; Amir Khusrau is credited with qawwali and the sitar.

q.s: Who founded the Rishi order of Sufis in Kashmir?
q.x: Sheikh Nuruddin (Nund Rishi) founded the Rishi movement of Kashmir.

q.s: In the Mughal war of succession, Dara Shikoh suffered his final defeat in 1659 at which battle?
q.x: Dara was finally defeated at Deorai near Ajmer in March 1659; Shuja was beaten at Khajwa.

q.s: The Battle of Dharmat (1658) in the Mughal war of succession was fought near which city?
q.x: Dharmat, where Aurangzeb and Murad defeated the imperial army in April 1658, is near Ujjain in Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: The 'Golden Firman' of 1632 granting trading privileges to the English was issued by which ruler?
q.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah of Golconda issued the Golden Firman of 1632 for English trade at Golconda's ports.

q.s: During the Mughal period, the silver that flowed into India came mainly from which region?
q.x: Europeans paid in bullion, mostly silver from Spanish America, making India a 'sink of precious metals'.

q.s: Tulsidas belonged to which branch of the Bhakti movement?
o: Krishnamargi branch of the Saguna stream
Ramamargi branch of the Saguna stream
q.x: Tulsidas was a Rama bhakta of the Saguna stream; Kabir and Ravidas were Nirguna saints.

q.s: The Dadu Panth was founded by Dadu Dayal in which region?
q.x: Dadu Dayal founded the Dadu Panth in Rajasthan.

q.s: In Shivaji's administration, the village accountant was known as the:
q.x: The Kulkarni was the village accountant and the Patil the village head; Deshmukh and Deshpande worked at the pargana level.

q.s: Which Mughal emperor's farman of 1717 is called the 'Magna Carta' of the English East India Company?
q.x: Farrukhsiyar's farman of 1717 granted the Company duty-free trade in Bengal.

q.s: Thomas Best's naval victory over the Portuguese off Swally in 1612 led to the English factory at:
q.x: Best's victory at Swally (1612) led to the establishment of the Surat factory in 1613.

q.s: Edward Terry came to the court of Jahangir as the chaplain of which Englishman?
q.x: Edward Terry was the chaplain of Sir Thomas Roe; Ralph Fitch had visited Akbar's court in 1583.

q.s: Which Mughal emperor's governor Qasim Khan captured Hooghly from the Portuguese in 1632?
q.x: Qasim Khan, governor of Bengal under Shah Jahan, took Hooghly in 1632.

q.s: Which development of 1580 weakened Portuguese power in India?
o: Defeat by the Dutch at Chinsura
q.x: Portugal's union with Spain in 1580 drew it into Spain's wars and weakened its position in India.

q.s: What was the main objective of the English East India Company in its early years in India?
q.x: The early aim was eastern trade, especially spices and textiles; purchases were paid for with imported bullion.

q.s: The Battle of St. Thome (1746) during the First Carnatic War was fought between the French and:
q.x: At St. Thome a small French force defeated the large army of the Nawab of Carnatic, Anwaruddin.

q.s: Robert Clive's attack on Arcot in 1751 aimed to relieve Muhammad Ali, who was besieged at:
q.x: Clive's raid on Arcot was a diversion to relieve Muhammad Ali besieged at Trichinopoly by Chanda Sahib.

q.s: The Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 in the Godavari Agency area was led by:
q.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24.

q.s: Which of the following movements is known as the 'Ulgulan' (great tumult)?
o: Munda rising led by Birsa Munda
q.x: The Munda Ulgulan of 1899–1900 was led by Birsa Munda.

q.s: The Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaiming Queen Victoria as Empress of India was held during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Lytton held the 1877 Durbar; Curzon held the 1903 Durbar for Edward VII.

q.s: In which year was New Delhi formally inaugurated as the capital of British India?
q.x: New Delhi, designed by Lutyens and Baker, was inaugurated in 1931.

q.s: The Ilbert Bill of 1883 was introduced during the viceroyalty of which of the following?
q.x: Drafted by Law Member C.P. Ilbert under Ripon, it would have let Indian judges try Europeans.

q.s: The European agitation against the Ilbert Bill came to be known as the:
q.x: The European protest against the Ilbert Bill was called the 'White Mutiny'.

q.s: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced for the first time by which of the following?
q.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced separate electorates, which encouraged communalism.

q.s: India continued to be governed by the Government of India Act, 1935, as adapted, until which date?
q.x: The 1935 Act, as adapted, governed India until the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

q.s: The Paramahansa Mandali, which opposed caste distinctions, was founded in Bombay in 1849 by:
q.x: Dadoba Pandurang founded the Paramahansa Mandali in Bombay in 1849.

q.s: The Arya Samaj founded by Dayananda Saraswati sought religious and social reform based on:
q.x: The Arya Samaj sought revival and reform based on the authority of the Vedas.

q.s: The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay in which year?
q.x: The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1867; the Brahmo Samaj dates to 1828.

q.s: The Dharma Sabha, which opposed the abolition of sati, was founded by:
q.x: Radhakant Deb's Dharma Sabha defended orthodoxy and opposed the abolition of sati.

q.s: Who founded the Dev Samaj, which forbade alcohol and meat?
q.x: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj; Shiv Dayal Singh founded the Radhasoami Satsang.

q.s: The revolutionary book 'Bandi Jivan' was written by which of the following?
q.x: Sachindranath Sanyal wrote Bandi Jivan (1922); Barindra Kumar Ghosh wrote the manual Mukti Kon Pathe.

q.s: Who described the Lucknow Pact with the remark "Better two united fists than a thousand scattered fingers"?
q.x: The remark on the Lucknow Pact was Tilak's, not Annie Besant's.

q.s: 'The Philosophy of the Bomb', a reply to Gandhi's 'The Cult of the Bomb', was written by:
q.x: Bhagwati Charan Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb in reply to Gandhi's article in Young India (1930).

q.s: Who among the following wrote the essay 'Why I am an Atheist'?
q.x: Bhagat Singh wrote 'Why I am an Atheist' in jail; Bose wrote 'The Indian Struggle'.

q.s: Which of the following was Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India?
q.x: Champaran (1917) was the first Satyagraha in India; Ahmedabad saw his first fast and Kheda his first non-cooperation.

q.s: Which of the following leaders did NOT leave the Congress over the Non-Cooperation programme?
q.x: C.R. Das gave up his legal practice and joined the movement; Jinnah, Besant, B.C. Pal and Khaparde left the Congress.

q.s: Who was the Viceroy of India when the Quit India Movement was launched in August 1942?
q.x: Linlithgow was Viceroy in August 1942; Wavell took over only in October 1943.

q.s: Who was the premier of Bengal when riots broke out in Calcutta on Direct Action Day in 1946?
q.x: H.S. Suhrawardy, the Bengal premier, led the League's rally in Calcutta on 16 August 1946.

q.s: Gandhi suggested that after independence the Congress be wound up and converted into a:
q.x: In his last proposal Gandhi suggested turning the Congress into a Lok Sevak Sangh.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the forms of satyagraha used by Gandhi?
q.x: Satyagraha relies on ahimsa (soul force); its forms include non-cooperation, picketing, hartal and fasting, never armed resistance.

q.s: Who presided over the special session of the Andhra Mahasabha held at Guntur in 1918?
q.x: The Guntur special session of 1918 was presided over by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.

q.s: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 was signed mainly to allay the fears of which region?
q.x: The Sri Bagh Pact sought to remove Rayalaseema's fear of domination by the Circars.

q.s: When the Andhra State was formed in 1953, where was its High Court located?
q.x: In line with the Sri Bagh Pact, the capital went to Kurnool and the High Court to Guntur in 1953.

q.s: Who was the first Speaker of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly formed in 1956?
q.x: Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao, a Visalandhra advocate, was the first Speaker of the AP Assembly.

q.s: Article 371D, giving special provisions for Andhra Pradesh, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 32nd Amendment (in force 1 July 1974), following the Six-Point Formula, inserted Articles 371D and 371E.

q.s: Under the Six-Point Formula of 1973, the Mulki Rules were replaced by:
q.x: The Six-Point Formula replaced the Mulki Rules with a zonal system for public employment and education.

q.s: How many Union Territories does India have after the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu in 2020?
q.x: After the January 2020 merger India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories.

q.s: Which of the following Union Territories created in 2019 does NOT have a legislature?
q.x: Jammu and Kashmir, Delhi and Puducherry have legislatures; Ladakh does not.

q.s: The Junagadh inscription of Saka 72 (150 CE) belongs to which ruler?
q.x: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman I is dated Saka 72, i.e. 150 CE.

q.s: Which Satavahana ruler defeated Nahapana and restruck his silver coins?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Kshatrapa Nahapana and restruck his coins.

q.s: The Nasik Prashasti describing the achievements of Gautamiputra Satakarni was issued by:
q.x: The Nasik Prashasti was issued by Gautami Balasri, his mother.

q.s: The Vikrama Samvat era is reckoned from which of the following years?
q.x: Vikrama Samvat begins in 57/58 BC; the Saka era in 78 AD, the Kalachuri era in 248 AD and the Harsha era in 606 AD.

q.s: Satavahana inscriptions were mostly written in which language?
q.x: Satavahana inscriptions are in Prakrit in the Brahmi script.

q.s: The Amaravati inscription of Pulomavi II is notable because it contains the Telugu word:
q.x: The Amaravati inscription of Pulomavi II has 'Nagabu', considered among the earliest Telugu words.

q.s: Which Ikshvaku king is called the 'Ashoka of the South' for his patronage of Buddhism?
q.x: Virapurushadatta, the only Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism, is called the 'Ashoka of the South'.

q.s: The Ajanta caves were discovered in 1819 by which British officer?
q.x: The Ajanta caves were found in 1819 by John Smith during a hunt.

q.s: In which year was the Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list?
q.x: Mahabalipuram was inscribed in 1984; Ajanta and Ellora in 1983.

q.s: The Kannada poet Pampa's 'Vikramarjuna Vijaya' is also known as:
q.x: Vikramarjuna Vijaya is popularly called the Pampa Bharata; his Adipurana deals with Rishabhadeva.

q.s: Chellavva, who bore the title 'Gandharva-Vidya-Visarada', was the court singer of which Eastern Chalukya king?
q.x: Chellavva was the singer and dancer of Chalukya Bhima I's court.

q.s: Rajaraja Narendra of Vengi married Ammanga Devi, the daughter of which Chola king?
q.x: Rajaraja Narendra (crowned 1022) married Ammanga Devi, daughter of Rajendra Chola I.

q.s: Ksheerarama, one of the five Pancharama shrines of Andhra, is located at:
q.x: Ksheerarama is at Palakollu; Kumararama is at Samalkot and Amararama at Amaravati.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the Pancharama shrines?
q.x: The Pancharamas are Amararama, Draksharama, Somarama, Ksheerarama and Kumararama; Srisailam is a Jyotirlinga, not a Pancharama.

q.s: The 'Ranganatha Ramayanam', the first Telugu Ramayana in dwipada metre, was written by:
q.x: Gona Budda Reddy wrote the Ranganatha Ramayanam, also the first dwipada kavya.

q.s: Tikkana's first work, 'Nirvachanottara Ramayanam', was dedicated to:
q.x: Tikkana dedicated Nirvachanottara Ramayanam to the Nellore Telugu Choda ruler Manumasiddhi II.

q.s: The Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva, along with Choda Tikka, killed which Velanati ruler in 1210?
q.x: Ganapatideva killed Prithviswara in 1210, ending the Velanati kingdom, and took the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.

q.s: The Ramappa temple at Palampet was built during the reign of which Kakatiya ruler?
q.x: The Ramappa temple was built in 1213 by Recherla Rudra, general of Ganapatideva.

q.s: Ganapatideva made his brother-in-law Jayapa the commander of his elephant force with the title:
q.x: Jayapa, brother of Ganapati's queens Narama and Perama, was made Gajasahani (commander of elephants).

q.s: Who founded the Gajapati dynasty of Orissa, which expanded into Andhra in the 15th century?
q.x: Kapilendra (Kapileswara) founded the Gajapati line; he took Kondaveedu around 1450.

q.s: Which Gajapati ruler lost Udayagiri, Kondaveedu and Kondapalli to Krishnadevaraya?
q.x: Prataparudra Gajapati lost these forts to Krishnadevaraya's campaigns.

q.s: The Telugu work 'Amuktamalyada' was written by:
q.x: Krishnadevaraya himself wrote Amuktamalyada; Peddana wrote Manucharitra.

q.s: Krishnadevaraya founded the town of Nagalapuram in memory of:
q.x: Nagalapuram was named after his mother Nagala Devi.

q.s: The Shravanabelagola inscription of 1368 records the settlement of a dispute between Jains and Vaishnavas by:
q.x: Bukka I settled the Jain-Vaishnava dispute in 1368; Harihara II became king only in 1377.

q.s: Kumara Kampana, who destroyed the Madurai Sultanate, was the son of which ruler?
q.x: Kumara Kampana, son of Bukka I, overthrew Sambhuvaraya and then the Madurai Sultanate.

q.s: Which Aravidu ruler was called the 'Second Krishnadevaraya' and moved his capital to Chandragiri?
q.x: Venkatapati Raya II, called Second Krishnadevaraya, ruled from Chandragiri.

q.s: Venkatapati Raya II allowed which European power to trade at Pulicat?
q.x: He allowed the Dutch, not the Portuguese, to trade at Pulicat.

q.s: Which foreign traveller compared Vijayanagara to Rome, saying it was as large as Rome?
q.x: Domingo Paes said the city was as large as Rome; Abdur Razzaq said 'the eye has not seen' its like.

q.s: Abdur Razzaq came to Vijayanagara in 1443 as the envoy of which ruler?
q.x: Abdur Razzaq was the envoy of the Timurid Shah Rukh to the court of Devaraya II.

q.s: The Russian traveller Athanasius Nikitin visited which kingdom in the 15th century?
q.x: Nikitin (1469–74) visited the Bahmani kingdom under Muhammad Shah III.

q.s: The Kakatiya Kala Thoranam of the Warangal fort appears in the state emblem of:
q.x: The Kala Thoranam is in the Telangana state emblem, not that of Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: In which year did N.G. Ranga form the Krishikar Lok Party?
q.x: Ranga formed the Krishikar Lok Party in 1951; he later joined in founding the Swatantra Party in 1959.

q.s: The Savara tribe of Andhra Pradesh mainly lives in which districts?
q.x: Savara, Jatapu and Gadaba live in Srikakulam–Vizianagaram; Koya live in the Godavari region.

q.s: The Chenchu tribe of Andhra Pradesh is mainly found in which region?
q.x: The Chenchus live in the Nallamala hills.

q.s: Who founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha in 1937?
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha in Madras in 1937.

q.s: Who became the first woman Governor of Andhra Pradesh in 1977?
q.x: Sharda Mukherjee was the first woman Governor of AP (1977); Kumudben Joshi came later.

q.s: In which year did Andhra Pradesh amend the Hindu Succession Act to give daughters coparcenary rights?
q.x: The Hindu Succession (AP Amendment) Act, 1986 came well before the Central amendment of 2005.

q.s: The Sahitya Akademi Award is given for works in how many languages?
q.x: It covers the 22 Eighth Schedule languages plus English and Rajasthani, i.e. 24 languages.

q.s: The Telugu novel 'Veyi Padagalu' was written by:
q.x: Veyi Padagalu is by Viswanatha Satyanarayana, the first Telugu Jnanpith awardee.

q.s: 'Ramayana Vishavruksham', a critique of the Ramayana, was written by:
q.x: Ranganayakamma wrote Ramayana Vishavruksham from a Marxist-feminist standpoint.

q.s: The Nanda king ruling Magadha at the time of Alexander's invasion, called Agrammes by Greek writers, was:
q.x: Dhana Nanda was the ruler in 326 BCE; Chandragupta Maurya overthrew him around 321 BCE.

q.s: As per the Census of India, what is the minimum population required for a place to be classified as a census town?
q.x: A census town needs at least 5,000 people, a density of 400 per sq km and 75% of male main workers in non-farm work.

q.s: What is the minimum population density required for a place to qualify as a census town?
q.x: The density test for a census town is at least 400 persons per sq km.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency?
q.x: Article 325 provides a single general roll per constituency and bars exclusion on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.

q.s: The Jagan Mitra Mandali (1906), the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State, was founded by:
q.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma founded the Jagan Mitra Mandali in 1906.

q.s: In which year did Gandhi found the Harijan Sevak Sangh?
q.x: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh in 1932 and started the paper Harijan in 1933.

q.s: Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Indian Union in 1975 through which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim a full State; the 35th had made it an associate State.

q.s: The demand for a separate Bundelkhand State covers parts of Uttar Pradesh and:
q.x: Bundelkhand lies across Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

q.s: The Eight-Point Formula of 1969 on the Telangana issue was announced by which Prime Minister?
q.x: Indira Gandhi announced the 8-Point Formula in 1969; Shastri had died in 1966.

q.s: The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016 bars adolescents aged 14 to 18 years from employment in:
q.x: Adolescents are barred only from hazardous occupations and processes; children below 14 are barred from all work except family help in non-hazardous work.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State had the largest number of child labourers in the 5–14 age group?
q.x: Uttar Pradesh had the largest number of child workers in Census 2011, which counted about 10.1 million nationally.

q.s: TRYSEM, launched in 1979 as a component of IRDP, aimed at:
o: Providing housing to the rural poor
q.x: TRYSEM trained rural youth for self-employment; DWCRA was the IRDP sub-scheme for rural women.

q.s: The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) of 2008 was formed by merging PMRY with:
q.x: PMEGP merged PMRY and REGP and is implemented through KVIC; JRY (1989) had merged NREP and RLEGP.

q.s: As per NFHS-5, what percentage of children under five years in India are stunted?
q.x: Stunting is 35.5%, wasting 19.3% and underweight 32.1%; 57.0% is anaemia among women aged 15–49.

q.s: The e-Shram portal of the Government of India is meant for the registration of:
q.x: e-Shram is the national database of unorganised workers, linked to central schemes through a One-Stop Solution.

q.s: The October 2024 India–China understanding on patrolling in eastern Ladakh covered Depsang and:
q.x: The October 2024 understanding on Depsang and Demchok was endorsed at the Modi–Xi meeting in Kazan.

q.s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 was signed by Rajiv Gandhi and which Sri Lankan leader?
q.x: Rajiv Gandhi and J.R. Jayewardene signed the accord in July 1987.

q.s: Provincial councils in Sri Lanka under the 1987 Accord were set up through which amendment of Sri Lanka's Constitution?
q.x: The 13th Amendment created provincial councils; the accord also provided for merging the Northern and Eastern provinces.

q.s: Which of the following are the two non-member observer States at the United Nations?
o: Holy See and State of Palestine
State of Palestine and Western Sahara
q.x: The Holy See and the State of Palestine are the UN's two non-member observer States.

q.s: The Commission on the Status of Women, set up in 1946, is a functional commission of which UN organ?
q.x: The CSW is a functional commission of the Economic and Social Council.

q.s: Major decisions of the IMF require what share of the total voting power, which gives the US an effective veto?
q.x: Major IMF decisions need an 85% supermajority; the US holds about 16.5% of the votes.

q.s: Where is the Secretariat of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) located?
q.x: The IORA Secretariat is at Ebene, Mauritius; India holds its chair for 2025–27.

q.s: The 'Bangkok Vision 2030' was adopted at the 6th Summit (April 2025) of which regional grouping?
q.x: The 6th BIMSTEC Summit at Bangkok adopted the Bangkok Vision 2030 and a Maritime Transport Cooperation Agreement.

q.s: How many Schedules did the original Constitution of India contain when it was adopted?
q.x: The original Constitution had 395 Articles and 8 Schedules; there are 12 Schedules today.

q.s: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were added to the Constitution by which Amendment?
q.x: The original Constitution had no Fundamental Duties; the 42nd Amendment added Article 51A.

q.s: Which of the following provinces did NOT have a bicameral legislature under the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: The six bicameral provinces were Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces; Punjab was unicameral.

q.s: Which Act changed the designation of the Governor-General of Bengal to the Governor-General of India?
q.x: The Charter Act, 1833 created the Governor-General of India; the 1858 Act gave the title of Viceroy.

q.s: Who chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
q.x: Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee and the Advisory Committee; Nehru chaired the Union Constitution and Union Powers Committees.

q.s: The Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee of the Constituent Assembly was chaired by:
q.x: J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee under Patel's Advisory Committee.

q.s: Special provisions protecting Mizo religious and social practices and customary law are contained in which Article?
q.x: Article 371G concerns Mizoram; 371F concerns Sikkim and 371A Nagaland.

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment is popularly known as the 'Mini Constitution'?
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) made sweeping changes, including to the Preamble and Seventh Schedule, and added Part IVA.

q.s: During a National Emergency, the enforcement of which Articles cannot be suspended after the 44th Amendment?
q.x: Since the 44th Amendment, Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359.

q.s: Under which Article can a citizen move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
q.x: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court; Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Supreme Court's Aadhaar judgment (2018) is correct?
o: Aadhaar is mandatory for obtaining SIM cards
Private entities may use Aadhaar under Section 57
Aadhaar is not mandatory for opening bank accounts
q.x: The Court upheld the scheme 4:1 but held it not mandatory for bank accounts and SIM cards, struck down Section 57, and said Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship.

q.s: Which was the first State in India to bring a State Uniform Civil Code into force?
q.x: Uttarakhand's UCC came into force on 27 January 2025; Goa follows the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867.

q.s: How many judges heard the Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973, the largest bench of the Supreme Court?
q.x: Kesavananda was heard by 13 judges; Golaknath had 11 and Minerva Mills 5.

q.s: Which case struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 inserted by the 42nd Amendment?
q.x: Minerva Mills (1980) struck down Articles 368(4) and 368(5).

q.s: Which Constitutional Amendment was Parliament's response to the Supreme Court's verdict in the Golaknath case?
q.x: The 24th Amendment (1971) answered Golaknath; the 25th, replacing 'compensation' with 'amount', answered R.C. Cooper.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty listed under Article 51A?
q.x: Paying taxes is not listed; safeguarding public property and abjuring violence are in clause (i) and striving for excellence in clause (j).

q.s: M. Venkaiah Naidu, who served as Vice-President of India from 2017 to 2022, hails from which district?
q.x: Venkaiah Naidu is from Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: Who among the following Vice-Presidents of India served two full terms in that office?
q.x: Hamid Ansari served two full terms (2007–17); S. Radhakrishnan was the other Vice-President with two terms.

q.s: The President's power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session is provided under:
q.x: Article 123 is the President's ordinance power; Article 213 is the Governor's.

q.s: Under which Article does the President address both Houses at the first session after each general election?
q.x: Article 87 provides the special address; Article 86 is the general right to address either House.

q.s: Who chaired the Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Bofors deal in 1987?
q.x: B. Shankaranand chaired the Bofors JPC; P.C. Chacko chaired the 2G JPC.

q.s: Under Lok Sabha Rule 374A, a member causing grave disorder is automatically suspended for:
o: The rest of the day only
The rest of the Lok Sabha's term
Five sittings or the rest of the session
q.x: Rule 374A provides automatic suspension for five consecutive sittings or the rest of the session, whichever is less.

q.s: Who was the first Leader of the Opposition in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
q.x: Communist leader Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first Leader of the Opposition.

q.s: Who was the first Speaker of the residuary Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly after bifurcation (2014–19)?
q.x: Kodela Siva Prasada Rao was Speaker in 2014–19; Ayyanna Patrudu is the present Speaker.

q.s: In a hung Assembly, which of the following gets the first preference for government formation under the Sarkaria–Punchhi guidelines?
q.x: The order is a pre-poll alliance, then the single largest party, then a post-poll coalition.

q.s: When was President's Rule imposed for the first time in Andhra Pradesh after its formation in 1956?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh's first spell came in 1973 during the Jai Andhra movement; Andhra State had one in 1954–55.

q.s: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 limited the size of a State Council of Ministers to what share of the Assembly?
q.x: The cap is 15 per cent of the Legislative Assembly's strength, with a minimum of 12 Ministers; it also deleted the one-third split exception.

q.s: The original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in disputes between the Centre and the States is provided by:
q.x: Article 131 gives exclusive original jurisdiction; Article 136 deals with special leave to appeal.

q.s: The Supreme Court grants special leave to appeal from any court or tribunal under:
q.x: Article 136 provides special leave; Article 133 covers civil appeals on a High Court certificate.

q.s: Administrative tribunals for disputes on the service of public servants are provided for under which Article?
q.x: Article 323A provides administrative tribunals; Article 323B covers tribunals for other matters.

q.s: Under the parliamentary system of the Indian Constitution, the real executive power at the Union level lies with:
o: The Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister
q.x: The President is the nominal head; real executive power is with the Council of Ministers headed by the PM.

q.s: The first Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal, which gave its award in the 1970s, was headed by:
q.x: The first KWDT was headed by R.S. Bachawat; KWDT-II (2004), set up by the Centre, was headed by Brijesh Kumar.

q.s: In which year was the Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal constituted?
q.x: The Godavari Water Disputes Tribunal was constituted in 1969, the same year as the first Krishna tribunal.

q.s: The Indian Forest Service was created as an All India Service in which year?
q.x: Only the IAS and IPS were created with the Constitution; the Indian Forest Service came in 1966.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to create new All India Services?
q.x: Article 312 allows new All India Services, including an All India Judicial Service, on a Rajya Sabha resolution.

q.s: Officers of the All India Services are appointed by:
o: The Governor of the cadre State
q.x: AIS officers are recruited by the UPSC and appointed by the President, then allotted to State cadres.

q.s: A member of the UPSC can be removed on the ground of misbehaviour only after an enquiry by:
q.x: Under Article 317 the President refers misbehaviour to the Supreme Court, whose advice after enquiry is binding.

q.s: The three-stage Civil Services Examination of prelims, mains and interview was recommended by which committee in 1976?
q.x: The Kothari Committee (1976) recommended the three-stage pattern; the Satish Chandra Committee (1989) added the essay paper.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the CAG of India is correct?
o: He can enforce recovery of irregular expenditure
He audits local bodies' accounts only on the request of the President or Governor
He controls the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund
q.x: Unlike Britain's C&AG, India's CAG has no control over the issue of money and cannot disallow expenditure; he is only an Auditor General.

q.s: The cadre-controlling authority for the Indian Police Service is:
q.x: The IPS is controlled by the MHA; the IAS by DoPT and the Indian Forest Service by MoEFCC.

q.s: Since the 2019 amendment, members of the NHRC hold office for a term of:
o: 6 years or until the age of 65
3 years or until the age of 70
5 years or until the age of 70
5 years or until the age of 65
q.x: Since 2019 members serve 3 years or till 70, whichever is earlier, and may be reappointed.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that the President's action under Article 356 is subject to judicial review?
q.x: S.R. Bommai (1994) held Article 356 proclamations open to judicial review.

q.s: In which year was the Planning Commission replaced by NITI Aayog?
q.x: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

q.s: Which unit of NITI Aayog is responsible for monitoring and evaluation of government programmes?
q.x: The DMEO monitors and evaluates programmes; the Team India Hub handles engagement with the States.

q.s: Which Prime Minister headed a minority Congress government that nevertheless completed its full term?
q.x: Narasimha Rao's minority government (1991–96) completed its full term.

q.s: Which Prime Minister's government of May 1996 lasted only 13 days?
q.x: Vajpayee's first BJP government in 1996 lasted 13 days.

q.s: Who chaired the Delimitation Commission of 2002?
q.x: The 2002 commission was chaired by Kuldip Singh; Ranjana Desai chaired the J&K commission of 2020.

q.s: Which Article provides for the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha?
q.x: Article 330 covers the Lok Sabha and Article 332 the State Assemblies.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the State Election Commission for Panchayat elections?
q.x: Article 243K provides the SEC; 243D deals with reservation, 243E with the term and 243ZD with the District Planning Committee.

q.s: What share of seats in Panchayats is reserved for women in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Article 243D requires at least one-third; Andhra Pradesh gives 50 per cent.

q.s: Which committee described the Panchayati Raj Institutions of its time as 'grass without roots'?
q.x: The G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985) used the phrase and made the district the basic unit of planning.

q.s: Grants recommended by the Union Finance Commission for Panchayats are based on which Article?
q.x: Local-body grants rest on Article 280 and are routed through the States; Article 270 covers the divisible pool.

q.s: Which was the first State in India to reserve 50 per cent of Panchayat seats for women, in 2006?
q.x: Bihar was first in 2006; about half of all elected PRI representatives in India are now women.

q.s: The tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram are administered under which Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: These four States come under the Sixth Schedule (Article 244(2)); the Fifth Schedule covers Scheduled Areas elsewhere.

q.s: Under the Sixth Schedule, who has the power to organise and re-organise the autonomous districts?
q.x: The Governor organises autonomous districts; there are ten, in Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Tripura.

q.s: Tribes India outlets and MSP for minor forest produce are run by which body?
q.x: TRIFED (1987) runs Tribes India and the MSP for MFP scheme.

q.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation, which procures minor forest produce from tribals, functions in which State?
q.x: The GCC of Andhra Pradesh (1956) buys MFP at fair prices and runs PDS depots in tribal areas.

q.s: Appeals against orders of the Data Protection Board of India lie with:
q.x: Under the DPDP Act, 2023 appeals go to the TDSAT within 60 days, then to the Supreme Court.

q.s: Which body fixes the ceiling prices of essential medicines and medical devices like coronary stents in India?
q.x: The NPPA capped stent prices in February 2017.

q.s: On which date was the scheme under the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act launched?
q.x: Parliament passed the Act on 23 August 2005; the scheme was launched on 2 February 2006.

q.s: How many days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household per year does MGNREGA provide?
q.x: MGNREGA guarantees 100 days of unskilled wage work per rural household in a year.

q.s: The DBT Mission, which coordinates Direct Benefit Transfer, is located in:
q.x: The DBT Mission sits in the Cabinet Secretariat; DBT was piloted from 1 January 2013.

q.s: The 'Badikosta' scheme of Andhra Pradesh provides which of the following?
q.x: Badikosta (2017) gives bicycles to Class IX girls; Vidya Kanuka provides free school kits.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh, Village Health Clinics have been set up at the level of the:
q.x: About 10,032 Village Health Clinics function at the village secretariat level.

q.s: The AP Employment of Local Candidates in Industries/Factories Act, 2019 reserves what share of private jobs for locals?
q.x: The 2019 Act reserved 75% of jobs in industries and factories for local candidates, the first such law in India.

q.s: In Andhra Pradesh's MGNREGS work in 2025–26, women accounted for about what share of total person-days?
q.x: Women made up about 60.54 per cent of person-days; AP ranked third nationally.

q.s: The 'Stree Shakti' scheme launched by Andhra Pradesh in August 2025 provides:
q.x: Stree Shakti gives free bus travel to women and transgender persons; Mission Shakti runs One Stop Centres and the 181 helpline.

q.s: The first regular synchronous Census of India in 1881 was conducted under which Viceroy?
q.x: The 1881 Census was held under Ripon; the non-synchronous Census of 1872 under Lord Mayo.

q.s: Which of the following sectors was found by the RBI study of 2014 to have negative employment elasticity?
q.x: Employment elasticity was negative in agriculture; construction and services were the most employment-intensive.

q.s: Article 31C, which protects laws giving effect to Articles 39(b) and 39(c), was inserted by:
q.x: The 25th Amendment (1971) inserted Article 31C.

q.s: Who developed a list of 'central capabilities' extending Amartya Sen's capability approach?
q.x: Martha Nussbaum gave the list of central capabilities; Mahbub ul Haq devised the HDI.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four pillars of human development?
q.x: The four pillars are Equity, Sustainability, Productivity and Empowerment.

q.s: Which regions of Andhra Pradesh lag behind in the State's intra-State development disparities?
q.x: Rayalaseema and North Coastal districts lag; the delta districts are the better-off areas.

q.s: What share of the divisible pool of central taxes did the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommend for the States?
q.x: The 16th FC kept the States' share at 41% for 2026–31, rejecting the demand for 50%.

q.s: Who is the Chairman of the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
q.x: Arvind Panagariya chairs the 16th FC; N.K. Singh chaired the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th.

q.s: Which instrument forms the floor of the RBI's liquidity adjustment facility corridor since April 2022?
q.x: The SDF absorbs surplus liquidity without collateral and is the floor; the MSF is the ceiling.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) is correct?
o: They are part of the payment and settlement system like banks
They cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves
They have direct access to the RBI's repo window
Their deposits are insured by DICGC
q.x: NBFCs cannot issue cheques on themselves, their deposits have no DICGC cover, and they cannot use the LAF window.

q.s: Under Basel III norms, the Liquidity Coverage Ratio requires banks to hold enough liquid assets to survive:
q.x: LCR covers a 30-day stress scenario; the Net Stable Funding Ratio covers a one-year horizon.

q.s: The Basel Committee on Banking Supervision works under which institution?
q.x: The BCBS, set up in 1974 after the failure of Bankhaus Herstatt, works under the BIS at Basel.

q.s: Gradual inflation that stays below about 3 per cent a year is known as:
q.x: Creeping inflation is below about 3%; walking inflation is 3–10% and galloping inflation is double or triple digit.

q.s: Which of the following types of inflation is the most severe in terms of the speed of price rise?
q.x: In ascending order of speed: creeping, walking, galloping and hyperinflation.

q.s: Repayment of loans by the government is treated as capital expenditure because it:
o: Reduces a liability of the government
q.x: Capital expenditure either creates assets or reduces liabilities; loan repayment reduces a liability.

q.s: Besides the debt-GSDP ratio, which indicator is especially relevant for assessing the debt sustainability of States?
o: Interest payments to revenue receipts ratio
q.x: Interest payments as a share of revenue receipts and debt-GSDP are the key State debt sustainability ratios.

q.s: The system of ad hoc Treasury Bills, used to monetise the Union deficit, was abolished with effect from:
q.x: Under the 1994 RBI–Government agreement, ad hoc Treasury Bills were abolished from 1 April 1997.

q.s: The concept of 'Effective Revenue Deficit' was first introduced in the Union Budget of:
q.x: ERD was introduced in Budget 2011-12 and added to the FRBM Act by the 2012 amendment.

q.s: The FRBM Bill was introduced in Parliament in 2000 by which Finance Minister?
q.x: Yashwant Sinha introduced the FRBM Bill; the Act was enacted in 2003 and came into force on 5 July 2004.

q.s: Service tax was introduced in India in 1994-95 on the recommendation of which committee?
q.x: Service tax began in 1994-95 on the Raja Chelliah Committee's advice; GST replaced it in 2017.

q.s: VAT is often described as a 'self-enforcing' tax mainly because of:
o: Collection at the first stage only
Input tax credit based on tax invoices
q.x: Input tax credit depends on the seller's tax invoice, so buyers demand proper invoices along the chain.

q.s: GST in India is based on which principle of taxation, benefitting consuming States like Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Under the destination principle the State share of IGST goes to the State where goods or services are consumed.

q.s: The LEADS (Logistics Ease Across Different States) index is released by:
o: DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
q.x: LEADS is released by DPIIT; in LEADS 2025 Tamil Nadu was an 'Exemplar' and AP an 'Accelerator'.

q.s: Software Technology Parks (STPs) under the export promotion schemes of India are meant for units dealing in:
q.x: STPs cover software and EHTPs electronics hardware; like EOUs they can be set up anywhere in India.

q.s: The Targeted Public Distribution System, with differential prices for BPL and APL families, was introduced in:
q.x: TPDS came in June 1997; the Revamped PDS of 1992 targeted remote and backward blocks.

q.s: In which Five-Year Plan were buffer stocks of foodgrains formally introduced?
q.x: Buffer stocks were formally introduced in the Fourth Plan.

q.s: The first Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) in India was set up in 1974 at:
q.x: The first KVK came up at Puducherry in 1974, on the Mohan Singh Mehta Committee's recommendation.

q.s: Krishi Vigyan Kendras in India are funded by:
q.x: KVKs are 100% funded by ICAR and supervised through 11 ATARIs.

q.s: The Model Agricultural Land Leasing Act, 2016 was prepared by:
q.x: NITI Aayog prepared the Model Act; its drafting committee was headed by T. Haque.

q.s: Land Development Banks, now called Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Banks, mainly provide:
q.x: Land Development Banks give long-term credit; the first was set up at Jhang in 1920.

q.s: In the cooperative credit structure, the District Central Cooperative Bank mainly finances the:
q.x: The DCCB finances the PACS at the base of the short-term cooperative structure.

q.s: Buffer norms for the Central Pool stocks of foodgrains are fixed by:
q.x: Buffer norms are fixed by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs; the CACP recommends MSPs.

q.s: Which of the following statements about industry in Andhra Pradesh after 2014 is correct?
o: Bifurcation took away the Hyderabad industrial and services base
Industry has no target under the 2024-29 policy
Manufacturing contributes about half of GSDP
Manufacturing is the largest contributor to GSDP
q.x: Bifurcation left Hyderabad with Telangana; manufacturing gives only about 11% of AP's GSDP.

q.s: The idea of 'premature deindustrialisation' is associated with which economist?
q.x: Rodrik's premature deindustrialisation means manufacturing peaks at a lower income level than in early industrialisers.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a public sector unit in India's early industrial base?
q.x: Sindri, Chittaranjan and HMT were public-sector units; Tata Steel was in the private sector.

q.s: MUDRA, set up on 8 April 2015, is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
q.x: MUDRA is a SIDBI subsidiary; CGTMSE was also set up by the Government and SIDBI.

q.s: Under the MSMED Act, a buyer must pay a micro or small enterprise supplier within a maximum of:
q.x: Payment is due within 45 days; on delay the buyer pays compound interest at three times the RBI bank rate.

q.s: Which sector of India's economy contributes over half of GDP but employs only about a third of workers?
q.x: In 2021-22 services gave 53.89% of GDP but employed 33.80% of the workforce.

q.s: The long-term vision document 'Swarna Andhra @2047' was launched on which date?
q.x: Swarna Andhra @2047 was launched on 13 December 2024; Vision 2020 (1999) was the first such vision.

q.s: Which sub-sector was the fastest-growing in Andhra Pradesh's agriculture sector in 2024-25?
q.x: Crops grew 14.99% in 2024-25; fishing and aquaculture grew 11.29%.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the models under Andhra Pradesh's Zero Poverty-P4 initiative?
q.x: The P4 models are Adopt a Family, Adopt a Community and Fund a Need; it was launched on Ugadi, 30 March 2025.

q.s: The large rise in AP's Agriculture and Allied allocation in 2025-26 BE over 2024-25 RE is partly explained by:
q.x: The 2024-25 RE (₹6,192 crore) was far below the ₹12,514 crore budgeted, so the 128% rise is partly a base effect.

q.s: The site of the Polavaram Project now falls in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The site, earlier in West Godavari, is now in Eluru district; the main dam is earth-cum-rock fill.

q.s: The Polavaram Project is a multipurpose project on which river?
q.x: Polavaram is on the Godavari, about 42 km upstream of the Cotton Barrage, and has national project status.

q.s: Which committee dealt with the allocation of All India Services officers between AP and Telangana after bifurcation?
q.x: Pratyush Sinha handled AIS officers; Kamalanathan State employees, Sheela Bhide Schedule IX bodies and Dharmadhikari power employees.

q.s: The AP Disaster Recovery Project, funded by the World Bank, followed which cyclone?
q.x: The APDRP followed Cyclone Hudhud, which hit Visakhapatnam in October 2014.

q.s: In 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh ranked first in India in the production of:
q.x: AP ranked first in eggs in 2023-24; it was seventh in milk and fourth in meat (2024-25).

q.s: Under the AP Industrial Development Policy 2020-23, what share of APIIC land was earmarked for MSMEs?
q.x: MSMEs got 33% of APIIC land; 16.2% of plots were reserved for SC entrepreneurs.

q.s: Kopparthy in Kadapa district is a node of which industrial corridor?
q.x: Kopparthy is the AP node of VCIC; Krishnapatnam is the AP node of CBIC.

q.s: Dholera, a greenfield industrial smart city, is located in which State?
q.x: Dholera is in Gujarat on the DMIC; Shendra-Bidkin is in Maharashtra.

q.s: The Vizag–Chennai Industrial Corridor in Andhra Pradesh is being developed with assistance from:
q.x: VCIC is supported by the ADB with the Government of AP.

q.s: India's first 'Quantum Valley', under the National Quantum Mission, is being developed at:
q.x: Amaravati Quantum Valley focuses on areas including Quantum Key Distribution.

q.s: The present public grievance platform of the Andhra Pradesh government is called:
q.x: Prajavani came first, then Meekosam (2014-19) and Spandana (2019-24); PGRS is the current system.

q.s: The Global Innovation Index is published by which organisation?
q.x: WIPO publishes the GII; Switzerland topped GII 2025 and India ranked 38th.

q.s: The Gutenberg discontinuity separates which layers of the Earth's interior?
q.x: Gutenberg (~2,900 km) separates mantle and outer core; Moho separates crust and mantle, Lehmann outer and inner core.

q.s: The Conrad discontinuity lies between:
q.x: Conrad separates the upper (SIAL) and lower (SIMA) crust.

q.s: The absence of S-waves beyond about 103–105 degrees from the epicentre shows that the:
q.x: S-waves travel only through solids; their shadow zone shows the outer core is liquid.

q.s: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is an example of which type of volcano?
q.x: Mauna Loa is a shield volcano of fluid basalt; Fuji is a composite cone.

q.s: The horizontal transfer of heat by wind, as seen in the 'Loo' of north India, is called:
q.x: Advection is horizontal heat transfer; convection is vertical.

q.s: The atmosphere is mainly heated by which of the following?
q.x: The Earth absorbs short-wave insolation and re-radiates long-wave terrestrial radiation, which heats the atmosphere.

q.s: Temperature inversion is favoured by which of the following conditions?
o: Short summer nights with cloudy skies
Long winter nights with clear skies
q.x: Long nights, clear skies and calm dry air favour inversion, which causes fog, frost and smog.

q.s: Which greenhouse gas is commonly known as 'marsh gas'?
q.x: Methane is marsh gas; over 100 years its Global Warming Potential is about 28–36 times that of CO₂.

q.s: Which is the most abundant greenhouse gas in the Earth's atmosphere?
q.x: Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas and acts as a feedback.

q.s: Which river, which has built a huge mega-fan, is known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar'?
q.x: The Kosi shifts course often and has built a mega-fan; the Damodar was the 'Sorrow of Bengal'.

q.s: The river valley famous for its ravines and badlands in central India is that of the:
q.x: The Chambal valley is known for ravines and badlands formed by gully erosion.

q.s: Which is the largest district of Andhra Pradesh by area in the present set of 28 districts?
q.x: In the 28-district set YSR Kadapa is the largest; Prakasam was largest in the 26-district set.

q.s: In the 13-district Andhra Pradesh that existed until April 2022, the largest district by area was:
q.x: Anantapur was the largest of the old 13 districts.

q.s: The winter rainfall in north-west India is mainly caused by:
q.x: Western disturbances from the Mediterranean bring winter rain to north-west India.

q.s: Which ministry is the nodal ministry of the Government of India for drought management?
q.x: Agriculture is nodal for drought, pest attack, hailstorm and frost; the Crop Weather Watch Group monitors drought.

q.s: The Zanskar river joins the Indus at which place?
q.x: The Zanskar joins the Indus at Nimu, downstream of Leh.

q.s: The Indus cuts a deep antecedent gorge near which mountain peak?
q.x: The Indus cuts its antecedent gorge at Nanga Parbat before turning south.

q.s: The Prakasam Barrage on the Krishna river is located at:
q.x: The Prakasam Barrage is at Vijayawada; the Godavari's Cotton Barrage is at Dowleswaram near Rajamahendravaram.

q.s: The Right Main Canal of the Nagarjuna Sagar project is known as the:
q.x: The Jawahar Canal is the Right Main Canal; the Left Canal is the Lal Bahadur Canal.

q.s: The first priority for action of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) is:
q.x: Sendai has four priorities; the first is understanding disaster risk.

q.s: India launched the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) in 2019 at:
o: UN Climate Action Summit, New York
q.x: The CDRI was launched at the UN Climate Action Summit in New York in September 2019.

q.s: The nodal ministry for India's Deep Ocean Mission is the:
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
q.x: The MoES runs the mission, whose submersible Matsya 6000 is meant to carry three people to 6,000 m.

q.s: The Kalagarh dam on the Ramganga river is located in which State?
q.x: The Ramganga (Kalagarh) dam is in Uttarakhand.

q.s: The Indira Gandhi Canal of Rajasthan takes off from which barrage?
q.x: The canal starts at Harike, at the Sutlej–Beas confluence, and is fed in winter by the Pong dam.

q.s: The Gang Canal of Rajasthan was built in 1927 by which ruler?
q.x: Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner built the Gang Canal in 1927.

q.s: Which is the largest continuous tropical rainforest in the world?
q.x: The Amazon is the largest; the Congo basin is second.

q.s: Which is the largest terrestrial biome of the world?
q.x: The taiga (boreal coniferous forest) is the largest land biome.

q.s: Which is the oldest gold field of India?
q.x: Kolar in Karnataka is India's oldest gold field.

q.s: India's first private-sector gold mine after Independence, Swarnagiri (Jonnagiri), is in which district?
q.x: The Jonnagiri mine is in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district, run by GeoMysore Services.

q.s: The main constituent of biogas, produced by anaerobic digestion, is:
q.x: Biogas is 50–75% methane; producer gas is mainly carbon monoxide and nitrogen.

q.s: Which country has the largest proved oil reserves in the world?
q.x: Venezuela has the largest proved oil reserves; Russia has the largest proved gas reserves.

q.s: Which country is the largest producer of natural gas in the world?
q.x: The USA is the largest natural-gas producer.

q.s: Sugar mills in India are located close to the cane-growing areas mainly because sugarcane:
q.x: Cane loses weight in processing and dries after cutting, so mills locate near the fields.

q.s: The iron and steel industry of India is largely concentrated in which region near its raw materials?
q.x: Steel uses weight-losing raw materials, so it clusters near iron ore and coal of the Chota Nagpur region.

q.s: What was the slogan of the 1965-66 agitation for the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant?
q.x: 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' (Visakha Steel – Andhra's Right) was the slogan.

q.s: The first blast furnace of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant was named:
q.x: The first blast furnace was named Godavari.

q.s: The Kia Motors automobile plant in Andhra Pradesh is located in which district?
q.x: Kia's plant at Penukonda is in Sri Sathya Sai district; Sri City has Isuzu and Foxconn.

q.s: How many use-based categories are used in the Index of Industrial Production (IIP)?
q.x: The IIP has six use-based classes: primary, capital, intermediate, infrastructure/construction, consumer durables and consumer non-durables.

q.s: Orvakal, a node of the Hyderabad–Bengaluru Industrial Corridor, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Orvakal is in Kurnool; Kopparthy is in YSR Kadapa and Donakonda in Prakasam.

q.s: The AP Industrial Development Policy 4.0 (2024-29) targets total investment of:
q.x: Policy 4.0, notified in October 2024, targets Rs 30 lakh crore; MSME Policy 4.0 was notified separately.

q.s: The longest road tunnel in the world, the Laerdal tunnel, is located in:
q.x: Laerdal in Norway (24.5 km) is the longest road tunnel.

q.s: The longest artificial canal in the world is the:
q.x: China's Grand Canal from Beijing to Hangzhou is the longest artificial canal.

q.s: Which of the following statements about India's services sector is correct?
o: It is the largest recipient of FDI in India
It accounts for less than a third of GVA
India is the largest services exporter in the world
q.x: Services are over half of GVA, the top FDI recipient, employ about 62% of urban workers, and India is the 7th largest exporter.

q.s: The nodal agency at the national level for the PMEGP is:
q.x: PMEGP is implemented through the Khadi and Village Industries Commission.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which category forms the largest share of India's workers?
q.x: Other workers were 41.6%, agricultural labourers 30.0%, cultivators 24.6% and household industry 3.8%.

q.s: After the recent remeasurement, Andhra Pradesh has which rank in coastline length among Indian States?
q.x: AP's coast of about 1,053 km is third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: What is the present rank of Andhra Pradesh among Indian States by area?
q.x: With 1,62,970 sq km, Andhra Pradesh is the 7th largest State by area.

q.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju's rising of 1922–24 was mainly against:
o: The forest laws and the muttadari system
q.x: The Rampa rising targeted restrictive forest laws and the muttadari system in the agency areas.

q.s: Which of the following towns is a planned city founded after Independence?
q.x: Dispur, like Chandigarh and Gandhinagar, is a post-1947 planned town; Madurai is ancient and Jaipur medieval.

q.s: The city of Chandigarh was designed by which architect?
q.x: Le Corbusier designed Chandigarh; Lutyens planned New Delhi.

q.s: Which was the first municipal corporation established in India in 1688?
q.x: Madras became India's first municipal corporation in 1688.

q.s: The 'Laws of Migration' (1885) were put forward by:
q.x: Ravenstein gave the laws of migration; Lee gave the push-pull theory and Zelinsky the mobility transition.

q.s: The 'push-pull' theory of migration (1966) is associated with:
q.x: Everett Lee gave the push-pull theory; Thompson and Notestein are linked with demographic transition.

q.s: B.S. Guha's racial classification of the Indian people was based on which Census?
q.x: Guha's classification of six groups used the 1931 Census; Risley's was based on 1901.

q.s: Which of the following tribes belongs to the Negrito racial group in India?
q.x: The Onge, Jarawa and Great Andamanese are Negrito; Santhal and Bhil are Proto-Australoid and Nagas Mongoloid.

q.s: Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for linguistic minorities is provided under:
q.x: Article 350A deals with mother-tongue instruction; 350B provides the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

q.s: In developed countries, services contribute roughly what share of GDP?
q.x: Services form about 70–80% of GDP in developed economies, where quaternary and quinary activities are expanding.

q.s: Which lake is the largest wintering ground for migratory waterfowl in the Indian subcontinent?
q.x: Chilika in Odisha is the largest wintering ground for migratory waterfowl.

q.s: In which year was the Indian peafowl declared the national bird of India?
q.x: The Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus) became the national bird in 1963.

q.s: Which is the only elephant reserve of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Rayala ER, which includes Koundinya WLS, is AP's only elephant reserve; Seshachalam is its biosphere reserve.

q.s: Which State has the largest wild elephant population in India as per the latest synchronous estimation?
q.x: Karnataka leads with about 6,013 elephants; India's total fell from 27,312 (2017) to 22,446 (2025).

q.s: In Weber's theory of industrial location, an industry with a Material Index greater than 1 tends to locate:
o: Midway between market and raw material
q.x: MI greater than 1 means weight-losing inputs, which pull the industry to the raw material; MI below 1 pulls it to the market.

q.s: The Hyogo Framework for Action (2005–2015) was adopted at which city?
q.x: The Hyogo Framework was adopted at Kobe; Yokohama gave the 1994 strategy and Sendai the 2015–2030 framework.

q.s: The UNESCO Kalinga Prize for the popularisation of science was instituted in 1952 with a donation from:
q.x: Biju Patnaik funded the Kalinga Prize; J.V. Narlikar won it in 1996.

q.s: Jainendra K. Jain, the first Indian-origin winner of the Wolf Prize in Physics (2026), is known for his work on:
q.x: Jain developed the theory of composite fermions in the fractional quantum Hall effect.

q.s: The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre began in 1954 under which original name?
q.x: AEET, Trombay (1954) was renamed BARC in 1967 after Homi Bhabha.

q.s: The Indian Veterinary Research Institute (IVRI) is located at:
q.x: IVRI is at Izatnagar, Bareilly; the Central Institute of Freshwater Aquaculture is at Bhubaneswar.

q.s: The National Institute of Biotic Stress Management of ICAR is located at:
q.x: Biotic stress management is at Raipur; the abiotic stress institute is at Malegaon, Baramati.

q.s: The satellite GSAT-N2 (GSAT-20), built by NSIL, was launched in November 2024 by:
q.x: GSAT-N2 was launched by Falcon 9; GSAT-24 had been launched by Ariane-5 from Kourou.

q.s: The Kapuluppada dump yard, where biomining of legacy waste is being done, is in which city?
q.x: GVMC is biomining legacy waste at Kapuluppada; Guntur's waste goes to the Jindal Waste-to-Energy plant.

q.s: IFFCO's Nano Urea is applied to crops mainly by which method?
q.x: Nano Urea is a liquid with 20–50 nm particles sprayed on leaves; its nitrogen-use efficiency is about 70%.

q.s: In October 2025, Google announced a $15 billion, 1 GW AI hub at which Indian city?
q.x: Google's AI hub is planned at Visakhapatnam, projected as India's biggest data-centre hub.

q.s: Which type of satellite is best suited for mapping floods through cloud cover?
q.x: SAR satellites like RISAT see through clouds; INSAT-3DS tracks cyclones and Oceansat helps fishing advisories.

q.s: Potential Fishing Zone advisories in India are issued by which body?
q.x: INCOIS, Hyderabad, issues PFZ advisories using data from satellites like EOS-06 (Oceansat-3).

q.s: The Pinaka multi-barrel rocket system was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
q.x: ARDE, Pune developed Pinaka; ADE, Bengaluru works on UAVs like Rustom and Lakshya.

q.s: Which DRDO laboratory at Hyderabad was the lead laboratory of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme?
q.x: DRDL led IGMDP; ASL works on the Agni series and DLRL on electronic warfare.

q.s: The vision of DRDO is to empower the nation with:
q.x: DRDO's vision is to empower India with indigenous defence and security technologies.

q.s: In India's nuclear command structure, which body alone can authorise the use of nuclear weapons?
o: Executive Council chaired by the NSA
Political Council chaired by the Prime Minister
q.x: The Political Council (PM) authorises use; the Strategic Forces Command (2003) manages and operates the arsenal.

q.s: The MRSAM (Barak-8) air defence missile was developed by DRDO jointly with:
q.x: MRSAM was developed by DRDO with Israel Aerospace Industries.

q.s: 'Akashteer', the automated air-defence control network, was built by:
q.x: Akashteer was built by Bharat Electronics Ltd with the Army; it is a control network, not a missile.

q.s: 'Prachand', inducted in October 2022, is India's:
q.x: LCH Prachand is HAL's light combat helicopter for high altitude; Dhruv is the Advanced Light Helicopter.

q.s: The Akash surface-to-air missile system is used by:
o: Both the Army and the Air Force
q.x: Akash serves both the Army and the Air Force; Akash-NG has a range of about 70 km.

q.s: The Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) aims at:
o: Rural digital literacy, one person per household
q.x: PMGDISHA targets digital literacy in rural areas, one person per household; e-Pathshala provides NCERT e-textbooks.

q.s: The SolarWinds incident of 2020 is an example of which type of cyber attack?
q.x: In a supply-chain attack a trusted vendor's software is compromised to reach its customers.

q.s: A deceptive e-mail that looks legitimate, sent to steal card details or passwords, is known as:
q.x: That is phishing; e-mail bombing floods one address with repeated mails.

q.s: KAMINI, located at Kalpakkam, is notable as the only reactor in India fuelled by:
q.x: KAMINI is fuelled by U-233; Dhruva is BARC's largest research reactor.

q.s: KRUSHAK, a radiation processing facility at Lasalgaon (Nashik), is mainly used for the irradiation of:
q.x: KRUSHAK at Lasalgaon irradiates onions to extend shelf life.

q.s: Sodium vapour lamps are preferred for street lighting in foggy areas because they:
o: Emit yellow light that does not scatter much in fog
Use the least power of all lamps
q.x: Sodium vapour lamps give yellow light that penetrates fog; mercury vapour lamps give white light.

q.s: About 94 per cent of India's biodiesel is produced from which feedstock?
q.x: Most of India's biodiesel comes from palm stearin, not jatropha; biodiesel is made by transesterification.

q.s: Carbon monoxide from vehicle exhaust is harmful because it:
o: Forms carboxyhaemoglobin and cuts oxygen supply
q.x: CO binds haemoglobin to form carboxyhaemoglobin; benzene is linked to leukaemia.

q.s: By which year was leaded petrol fully phased out in India?
q.x: Leaded petrol was fully phased out in India by 2000.

q.s: Which renewable energy source has the largest installed capacity in India?
q.x: Solar leads (about 165 GW in August 2026), followed by wind (about 58 GW) and large hydro (about 52 GW).

q.s: Which State has the largest installed wind power capacity in India?
q.x: Gujarat is first, followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka; Andhra Pradesh is sixth.

q.s: The Muppandal wind farm, one of India's largest onshore wind farms, is located in:
q.x: Muppandal is in Kanyakumari district; Khavda is in Kutch and Ramagiri in Ananthapuramu.

q.s: Which bacterium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants?
q.x: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically; Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter carry out nitrification.

q.s: The conversion of nitrate into nitrogen gas, called denitrification, is carried out by:
q.x: Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus denitrify nitrate back to N₂.

q.s: The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve of Andhra Pradesh was notified in which year?
q.x: Seshachalam was notified in 2010; it is home to the endemic cycad Cycas beddomei and red sanders.

q.s: In the IUCN Red List, the code 'NT' stands for:
q.x: NT is Near Threatened, a species close to qualifying for a threatened category.

q.s: A species whose effect on its ecosystem is disproportionately large relative to its numbers is called a:
q.x: Keystone species have outsized effects; flagship species are charismatic ones used to win public support.

q.s: What is the IUCN Red List status of the gharial?
q.x: The gharial is Critically Endangered; the Asiatic lion is Endangered and the one-horned rhino Vulnerable.

q.s: The concept of 'Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas' (IBAs) was developed by:
q.x: IBAs are a BirdLife International programme; biodiversity hotspots come from Conservation International.

q.s: The Appiko movement of Karnataka (1983) for forest conservation was led by:
q.x: Panduranga Hegde led the Appiko movement; Chipko began in 1973 in Chamoli district.

q.s: The National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources, which houses the National Gene Bank, is located at:
q.x: NBPGR is at New Delhi; NBAGR (livestock) is at Karnal and NBFGR (fish) at Lucknow.

q.s: The Central Zoo Authority was given statutory status by an amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act in:
q.x: The 1991 amendment to the WPA, 1972 provided for the CZA.

q.s: Which of the following Biosphere Reserves of India is NOT included in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves?
q.x: Seshachalam is outside the WNBR along with Manas and Dibru-Saikhowa; 13 of India's 18 BRs are in it.

q.s: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, waste must be segregated at source into how many streams?
q.x: Waste is segregated into wet, dry, sanitary and special care streams.

q.s: The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) was created following which conference?
q.x: The 1972 Stockholm Conference created UNEP; the 1992 Earth Summit adopted Agenda 21.

q.s: The outcome document of the Rio+20 conference of 2012 is titled:
q.x: Rio+20 produced 'The Future We Want'; 'Our Common Future' is the Brundtland Report (1987).

q.s: The Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of clean, unpolluted water is generally below:
q.x: Clean water has BOD below 4 mg/L; higher BOD indicates organic pollution.

q.s: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards are notified under which Act?
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
q.x: The NAAQS, covering 12 pollutants, come under the Air Act.

q.s: On which date did Bharat Stage VI emission norms come into force across India?
q.x: India leapfrogged from BS-IV to BS-VI on 1 April 2020.

q.s: UNEP launched its Green Economy Initiative in which year?
q.x: UNEP's Green Economy Initiative came in 2008, before Rio+20; PAGE followed in 2013.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT covered under India's Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regimes listed here?
q.x: EPR covers plastic packaging, e-waste, batteries and tyres; crop residue is not an EPR product.

q.s: Who first proposed the concept of the greenhouse effect in the 1820s?
q.x: Fourier proposed the idea in the 1820s; Tyndall and Arrhenius developed it later.

q.s: Without the natural greenhouse effect, the Earth's average surface temperature would be about:
q.x: Without it the average would be about −18°C instead of +15°C; the greenhouse effect adds about 33°C.

q.s: According to the IPCC Special Report on 1.5°C, what share of coral reefs would be lost at 2°C of warming?
q.x: At 1.5°C, 70–90% of reefs would be lost; at 2°C more than 99%.

q.s: Which Working Group of the IPCC deals with the mitigation of climate change?
q.x: WG I covers the physical science basis, WG II impacts and adaptation, and WG III mitigation.

q.s: Under the New Collective Quantified Goal agreed at COP29, developed countries are to mobilise at least how much a year by 2035?
q.x: The core goal is US$300 billion a year by 2035; the broader US$1.3 trillion goal is aspirational. India called it inadequate.

q.s: The idea of the Sustainable Development Goals was first proposed at Rio+20 by which two countries?
q.x: Colombia and Guatemala proposed the SDGs at Rio+20 (2012).

q.s: The SDGs were adopted in 2015 at which session of the UN General Assembly?
q.x: The 2030 Agenda with 17 SDGs was adopted at the 70th UNGA session in September 2015.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Quadripartite on One Health?
q.x: The Quadripartite is WHO, FAO, UNEP and WOAH; UNICEF is not part of it.

q.s: The National Institute of One Health of India is located at:
q.x: The National Institute of One Health is at Nagpur.

q.s: Who discovered streptomycin, the first effective anti-tuberculosis drug?
q.x: Waksman discovered streptomycin; Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928.

q.s: 'MERA' is an ICMR initiative aimed at the elimination of which disease?
q.x: MERA is the Malaria Elimination Research Alliance.

q.s: 'U-WIN' is India's digital platform for:
q.x: U-WIN registers and tracks vaccinations.

q.s: The National Sickle Cell Anaemia Elimination Mission was launched on 1 July 2023 at:
q.x: The Mission was launched at Shahdol and aims to eliminate the disease by 2047.

q.s: SDG target 3.1 seeks to reduce the global maternal mortality ratio to less than:
q.x: Target 3.1 aims for an MMR below 70 per 1,00,000 live births by 2030.

q.s: Under the International Health Regulations (2005), a possible Public Health Emergency of International Concern must be reported to WHO within:
q.x: Countries must notify WHO within 24 hours; the 2024 amendments added a higher 'pandemic emergency' tier.

q.s: SARS-CoV-2 enters human cells through which receptor?
q.x: SARS-CoV-2 binds the ACE2 receptor; HIV uses CD4.

q.s: Under PM CARES for Children, a child orphaned by COVID-19 receives a lump sum of Rs 10 lakh at the age of:
q.x: The scheme, launched on 29 May 2021, gives a monthly stipend from 18 and Rs 10 lakh at 23.

q.s: 'eSanjeevani' under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission is a:
q.x: eSanjeevani is the national telemedicine service; ABHA is the health ID.

q.s: The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) functions under which department?
o: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
q.x: CSIR is under DSIR; its Director-General is also Secretary, DSIR.

q.s: The two defence industrial corridors of India are located in Uttar Pradesh and:
q.x: The defence industrial corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

q.s: Who is the Chairperson of SEBI who announced a regulated venue for pre-listing trades in August 2025?
q.x: Tuhin Kanta Pandey, SEBI Chairperson, made the announcement at FICCI on 21 August 2025.

q.s: In June 2025 the RBI's MPC cut the repo rate by 50 basis points to:
q.x: The repo was cut to 5.50% on 6 June 2025, and the stance changed from accommodative to neutral.

q.s: The 26th SCO Council of Heads of State, marking its 25th anniversary in 2026, was held at:
q.x: The summit was at Bishkek under President Sadyr Japarov; Pakistan was named the next chair.

q.s: The IndiaAI Mission, approved in March 2024, is implemented by which ministry?
o: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
q.x: MeitY implements the IndiaAI Mission (outlay Rs 10,371.92 crore).

q.s: The Permanent Court of Arbitration, set up in 1899, is headquartered at:
q.x: The PCA is at The Hague; the IPU is at Geneva and the CPA in London.

q.s: The Secretariat of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is located at the headquarters of the:
q.x: The FATF, set up by the G7 in 1989, has its Secretariat at the OECD in Paris.

q.s: The 'Dunkel Draft' is associated with which round of multilateral trade negotiations?
q.x: Arthur Dunkel's 1991 Draft Final Act was for the Uruguay Round of GATT.

q.s: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023, India was ranked:
q.x: India ranked 38th of 139 countries in LPI 2023.

q.s: The Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement (CCRA), in which India chairs a board, deals with:
o: Mutual recognition of IT security certificates
q.x: CCRA covers IT security certification; MeitY and STQC are India's certification authorities.

q.s: India became the world's fourth-largest economy in 2025, overtaking which country?
q.x: India passed Japan in 2025 with nominal GDP of about $4.18 trillion.

q.s: Which of the following currencies is NOT part of the IMF's SDR basket?
q.x: The SDR basket has the US dollar, euro, yuan, yen and pound sterling.

q.s: The Visakhapatnam-class (Project-15B) destroyers were built by:
q.x: MDL, Mumbai built the four P-15B destroyers.

q.s: The 570 MW Wangchhu Hydroelectric Project is located in which country?
q.x: Wangchhu is in Bhutan, a joint venture of Druk Green Power (51%) and Adani Power (49%).

q.s: 'Mission 500' aims to raise bilateral trade to USD 500 billion by 2030 between India and:
q.x: Mission 500 is the India–US trade target.

q.s: In April 2025, the Indian Navy contracted how many Rafale-M jets for its carriers?
q.x: The Navy ordered 26 Rafale-M jets; the IAF had bought 36 Rafales under the 2016 deal.

q.s: Under the semiconductor Design Linked Incentive (DLI) scheme, the incentive is linked to:
o: Net sales, for up to 5 years
q.x: The DLI scheme gives an incentive on net sales for up to 5 years; Semicon 2.0 has six pillars from design to talent.

q.s: 'Meera Behn', after whom an Indian Coast Guard ship was named, was the Indian name of:
q.x: Madeleine Slade, a disciple of Gandhi, was called Meera Behn; Margaret Noble was Sister Nivedita.

q.s: The Varunastra torpedo, developed by DRDO, is a:
q.x: Varunastra is a ship-launched heavyweight anti-submarine torpedo developed by DRDO and made by BDL.

q.s: Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL), a defence PSU making missiles and torpedoes, is headquartered at:
q.x: BDL is headquartered at Hyderabad.

q.s: The Arnala-class anti-submarine shallow water craft of the Indian Navy are built by:
q.x: Arnala-class craft are built by GRSE and Mahe-class by Cochin Shipyard; the programme has 16 vessels.

q.s: The National Digital Library of India (NDLI) is maintained by:
q.x: NDLI is maintained by IIT Kharagpur.

q.s: After the recent revision, what is the length of India's coastline?
q.x: The coastline was revised from 7,516.6 km to 11,098.81 km across 9 States and 4 UTs.

q.s: 'Vyommitra', associated with India's Gaganyaan mission, is a:
q.x: Vyommitra is a female humanoid that will fly on the uncrewed flight; Gaganyaan plans 3 astronauts at about 400 km.

q.s: 'SabhaSaar', an AI tool that uses BHASHINI, is designed to:
o: Prepare minutes of Gram Sabha meetings
q.x: SabhaSaar prepares AI-generated Gram Sabha minutes in 14 languages; BhuPRAHARI is a separate platform.

q.s: DHRUV64, India's indigenous 64-bit microprocessor developed by C-DAC, is based on which architecture?
q.x: DHRUV64 uses the open-source RISC-V architecture.

q.s: Who conducts the International Fleet Review of the Indian Navy in his capacity as Supreme Commander?
q.x: The President, as Supreme Commander of the armed forces, reviews the fleet.

q.s: Project 17A of the Indian Navy is a follow-on of which class of frigates?
q.x: Project 17A follows the Project 17 (Shivalik-class) frigates; MDL builds four and GRSE three.

q.s: The Paris Agreement on climate change was adopted at which Conference of the Parties?
q.x: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 in 2015; NDCs are updated every five years.

q.s: Under the Paris Agreement, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are to be updated every:
q.x: Countries submit new or updated NDCs every five years; the Global Stocktake only assesses collective progress.

q.s: UNESCO, which released the Global Report on Teachers in 2026, is headquartered at:
q.x: UNESCO was established on 16 November 1945 and is headquartered in Paris.

q.s: According to a 2024 study, which country has contributed the most to global warming so far?
q.x: The USA (about 0.27°C) leads, followed by China, Russia and India.

q.s: UNCTAD's Trade and Development Report 2026 projected India's GDP growth for 2026 at:
q.x: UNCTAD projected 7.3% for India, the fastest among major economies.

q.s: The Aspirational Districts Programme of NITI Aayog, launched in January 2018, covers how many districts?
q.x: The ADP covers 112 districts and works on Convergence, Collaboration and Competition.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an indicator used in the Global Hunger Index?
q.x: The GHI uses undernourishment, child wasting, child stunting and under-five mortality.

q.s: On the Global Hunger Index scale of 0 to 100, which score indicates the best situation (no hunger)?
q.x: Zero is the best score on the GHI; higher scores mean more hunger.

q.s: Who was the first Indian to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize?
q.x: Balkrishna Doshi won it in 2018; Zaha Hadid (2004) was the first woman winner.

q.s: Gerd Faltings, winner of the Abel Prize 2026, is famous for proving which conjecture?
q.x: Faltings proved the Mordell Conjecture; Perelman proved the Poincaré Conjecture.

q.s: The National Energy Conservation Awards are presented every year on 14 December, observed as:
q.x: NECA, instituted in 1991 by the Ministry of Power, is presented on National Energy Conservation Day.

q.s: Prof. K.L. Krishna, Padma Shri awardee, led the India KLEMS productivity project at which institution?
q.x: He led India KLEMS at the Delhi School of Economics; he hails from Unguturu in Krishna district.

q.s: The Subhash Chandra Bose Aapda Prabandhan Puraskar is given for excellence in which field?
q.x: It honours disaster management work and is announced on 23 January, Parakram Diwas.

q.s: Who was the first recipient of the Jnanpith Award in 1965?
q.x: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam) received the first Jnanpith.

q.s: For which work did Viswanatha Satyanarayana, the first Telugu recipient, receive the Jnanpith Award?
q.x: Viswanatha got it in 1970 for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu; C. Narayana Reddy won it in 1988 for Viswambhara.

q.s: Who became the youngest Formula 1 World Champion in 2026?
q.x: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli became the youngest champion at 20, clinching it at the Mexico City GP.

q.s: 'Kadha Rasa Sangama' was the theme of which cultural event held in 2026?
q.x: The 17th Kathakali Festival in Chennai had the theme Kadha Rasa Sangama.

q.s: The Chennakeshava temple at Belur was built by which Hoysala ruler?
q.x: Vishnuvardhana built the Chennakeshava temple at Belur; the Somanathapura temple is a 13th-century trikuta.

q.s: The Ol Chiki script, which completed a century in 2026, was created for which language?
